introduction: On this second Sunday of Advent, Isaiah announces a shoot from the stump of Jesse, on whom the Spirit of the Lord will rest, and a world where the wolf lives with the lamb. In the Gospel, John the Baptist appears in the desert, calling people to repent and to prepare the way of the Lord. Paul urges us to welcome one another as Christ welcomed us. Let us prepare our hearts for the coming of the Lord.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord comes to bring justice and peace. Let us bring him our prayers as we prepare his way.
intentions: For the Church: that she may prepare the way of the Lord by calling all people to repentance. Let us pray to the Lord.
For a world wounded by violence: that the peace of the Messiah may reconcile enemies. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor and the oppressed: that they may receive justice from the one on whom the Spirit rests. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our communities: that we may welcome one another as Christ has welcomed us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may bear fruit worthy of repentance this Advent. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way of your Son. Give us repentant hearts, and fill us with the hope of the peace he will bring. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Prepare the way of the Lord
reflection.body:
Isaiah begins with an image of hope from something that seems dead: "A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse." The royal line of David has been cut down like a tree, but new life will spring from the stump. On this new king, "The LORD's Spirit will rest": wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge and fear of the Lord. The Church has seen in these the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

This king will bring justice to the poor, and his reign will bring a peace so deep that creation itself is healed: "The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat... and a little child will lead them." This is the world God is preparing.

In the Gospel, John the Baptist appears in the desert, dressed in camel's hair, eating locusts and wild honey. His message is simple: "Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!" Matthew sees in him the voice Isaiah foretold: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness, make the way of the Lord ready! Make his paths straight!"

Crowds come to be baptized, confessing their sins. But John has strong words for religious leaders who come without real conversion: "produce fruit worthy of repentance!" Being a descendant of Abraham is not enough. Conversion must show itself in life.

Then John points to someone greater: "he who comes after me is mightier than I... He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit."

Paul gives us a practical way to prepare: "accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you." Advent is a time to welcome others, even those we find difficult.

This week, prepare the way of the Lord: go to confession before Christmas, and make peace with someone you are at odds with.
